_comment: Measured on this box, not assumed. Every number here was produced by a run whose command is named. The feasibility stage scores candidate experiments against this.

container.note: cgroup limits (memory.max=8589934592, cpu.max=200000/100000). The HOST has 24 cores and 226 GiB and none of it is reachable. Kubernetes pod.

load_7b_bf16.verdict: works, but AT the ceiling. Load one model at a time and free it before the next.

generation.note: Budget SHORT generations from the batched tok/s figure. Budget LONG generations from long_generation_cost_model instead: it is step-bound, not throughput-bound.

long_generation_cost_model._why_this_matters: The 3003.8 tok/s figure was measured on 512-token generations and does NOT transfer to long ones. Greedy decoding to a cap of N is N SEQUENTIAL forward passes; wall-clock is (number_of_batches x max_new_tokens x per_step_latency), and token throughput is a derived quantity, not the driver.
long_generation_cost_model.consequence: Increasing batch_size is nearly FREE for long generations: the step count is fixed by max_new_tokens, so a bigger batch amortises the same steps over more sequences. Batch 8 at an 8192 cap wastes most of the GPU.
long_generation_cost_model.observed: A calibration pass of 32 sequences at an 8192 cap, run as 4 batches of 8, took about 16 minutes wall-clock including two model loads -- consistent with ~25-30 ms per step at batch 8. The same 32 sequences as one batch of 32 would have been roughly a quarter of that.
long_generation_cost_model.second_consequence: HF generate stops only when EVERY sequence in the batch has emitted EOS, so one long trace holds the whole batch at the cap. Give a reasoning model and an instruct model separate caps and separate batches rather than mixing them, and prefer larger batches of similar-length work.
long_generation_cost_model.status: inferred from a live calibration run, not from a dedicated sweep -- the per-step latency vs batch curve has not been measured directly

attention_microbench.note: No model weights needed. The cheapest way to use this GPU.

consequences: No Codex CLI, so ARIS's cross-model reviewer is unavailable; bin/repro-gate.py stands in for it.
No cron/systemd: the unattended loop is flock + nohup.
vLLM is NOT installed and is risky here: its CPU-side work and RAM appetite do not fit 2 cores / 8 GiB comfortably. Use transformers with batching.

filesystem.metadata_io: very slow -- `du` over $HOME hangs. Do not create tens of thousands of small files.

hard_limits: A 14B model in bf16 will NOT load: 7B already peaks the 8 GiB cgroup.
No training, no fine-tuning of anything above ~1B, no multi-GPU.
No CPU-heavy data processing: 2 cores. Corpus-scale preprocessing is out.
No concurrency for speed: parallel processes on 2 cores make things slower.
Network egress works (github, arxiv, huggingface, pypi all reachable).

budget.note: A submission window is ~7 days. Aim each experiment at under 6 hours so the sweep can be repeated after the pilot finds bugs.
